h: וַיֵּלֶךְ וְשַׁבַּת תְּשׁוּבָה, ו׳ Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah, 6

p: Behold, our Sages of blessed memory instituted
that on Shabbos one does not pray
because its blessings are for a person's own needs.
Now seemingly, the first weekday blessing,
שֶׁהוּא אַתָּה חוֹנֵן לְאָדָם דַּעַת וְכוּלֵּי
which is "You graciously grant man knowledge," etc.,
"and graciously grant us from You," etc.,
that one should have the true knowledge
to recognize the revelation of the Creator, blessed be His Name,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כח, ט)
דַּע אֶת אֱלֹהֵי אָבִיךָ וְעָבְדֵהוּ וְגוֹמֵר.
"Know the God of your father and serve Him," etc.
וַהֲלֹא זֹאת אֵינוֹ לְצָרְכּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם;
Surely this is not for a person's own needs;
so why do we not pray
and grant our portion in Your Torah"?
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
along the lines of what our Rabbis of blessed memory said
it is as if the Beis HaMikdash were built in his days.
The Mikdash was placed between two Divine Names,
and knowledge was placed between two Divine Names."
That is: the meaning of da'as
is a recognition, in which one recognizes
he is surrounded by His providence, blessed be He.
And this is what is meant by its being placed
between two holy Names of Hashem.
Likewise, at the site of the Mikdash,
by the providence of His light, blessed be He,
in every detail of their affairs.
And this is what they, of blessed memory, said
מָה רָאוּ לוֹמַר בִּינָה אַחַר קְדֻשָּׁה?
"Why did they see fit to say Binah after Kedushah?
'And they shall sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov,' etc.,
'And those of errant spirit shall come to understanding.'"
That is: the blessing "You are holy"
הוּא כְּנֶגֶד בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם;
corresponds to the aspect of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him;
The first corresponds to the aspect of
Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him;
therefore we say, "Who bestows good kindnesses,"
for his attribute was that of love of kindness,
only to do kindness with people
and to instill in their hearts the love of Hashem.
כְּנֶגֶד בְּחִינַת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
corresponds to the aspect of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
to serve Hashem, blessed be He, with awe and dread,
Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, however,
לֹא הָיָה לוֹ בְּיִחוּד מִדָּה פְּרָטִית,
did not have one particular attribute specifically;
he was cleaving to Him, blessed be He.
Therefore even at the time of sleep
he was bound to Hashem, blessed be He,
"and behold, Hashem stood over him," etc.
And this is the aspect of kedushah,
"And they shall sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov."
And from this one comes to the aspect of da'as,
of His providence, blessed be He,
over every detail of a person's conduct
who are on this rung always;
but when the day of Shabbos arrives,
then Hashem, blessed be He, causes to shine forth
in all the souls of Yisrael,
"to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you."
That is: at that time each one recognizes
the light of His providence, blessed be He,
בְּכָל פְּרָטֵי עִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן,
in every detail of the affairs of this world as well,
so as to fulfill "In all your ways know Him"
And therefore the mitzvah of oneg Shabbos comes,
to take delight in food and drink as well,
and through this one will delight in Hashem.
and to ask for the gracious gift of da'as,
with which Hashem, blessed be He, has graced us
in the holiness of the day of Shabbos,
in which the aspect of da'as shines forth
in the collective souls of Yisrael
רַק בַּחוֹל צְרִיכִים לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל זֶה,
Only on weekdays must we pray for this,
"and graciously grant us from You," etc.,
by way of the attribute of grace,
a free gift from Him, blessed be He,
for not every person merits this,
as they, of blessed memory, said,
כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דֵּעָה וְכוּלֵּי,
"Bring us back, our Father, to Your Torah," etc.,
of which they said in the Gemara (Megillah 17b, cited above):
מָה רָאוּ לוֹמַר תְּשׁוּבָה אַחַר בִּינָה?
"Why did they see fit to say Teshuvah after Binah?
'and his heart will understand, and he will repent and be healed'" —
For Hashem, blessed be He, says,
"Return to Me and I will return to you"
that Hashem, blessed be He, send into our hearts
But on the day of Shabbos,
when da'as shines forth in the souls of Yisrael from Above,
there comes of itself as well
an arousal of teshuvah in the heart,
as they, of blessed memory, said
כָּךְ הוּא כֹּחָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵּי;
"Such is the power of teshuvah," etc.;
he said, "A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos:
It is good to give thanks to Hashem"
"But he who confesses and forsakes shall obtain mercy."
And on the day of Shabbos the acknowledgment comes
which is the first Shabbos of the year,
when the power of teshuvah then sparkled forth
at the very onset of Shabbos,
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
"And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good";
even what to the eye's sight was
מִכָּל הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
than all the creation of the six days of Creation,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם רַק כִּי טוֹב לְבַד;
about which only "that it was good" is said;
אָמְנָם כָּאן נֶאֱמַר וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאוֹד,
but here it says, "and behold, it was very good,"
which indicates rectification out of the corruption,
וְעַל זֶה בִּיקֵּשׁ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And for this King David, peace be upon him, asked
"Wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow";
for snow is the utmost whiteness,
as in "a bahares as intensely white as snow"
Yet there is a further level
וְטוֹב מְאוֹד הַיְינוּ כֹּחַ הַבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה,
while "very good" is the power of baalei teshuvah,
when willful sins become like merits;
and these are on a still higher level,
as in their saying, of blessed memory
"In the place where baalei teshuvah stand,
And as is known from the parable of a king's son:
when he comes to his father
after having been far from him in captivity,
then the joy is far greater
than when he is with him in his house constantly.
the joy is increased all the more,
for "the bones You have crushed will rejoice":
through bitterness and brokenness of heart
עַתָּה עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְרַבָּה הַשִּׂמְחָה.
now through this the joy is increased.
וְזֶה מְרֻמָּז גַּם כֵּן בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת,
And this too is alluded to regarding the day of Shabbos,
where it says, "It is good to give thanks to Hashem";
that comes about from acknowledgment and teshuvah,
one comes "to sing to Your Name, O Most High."
the songs and the joy are increased,
from the very fact that one comes to recognize
for the intellect cannot comprehend this,
And therefore this Shabbos is called
which is like the beginning of Creation,
the light of teshuvah shines forth as it did then.
For the Ten Days of Teshuvah
within the Ten Days of Teshuvah
the light of Binah shines forth,
so that it be as it says,
"and his heart will understand, and he will repent and be healed."
וְגַם אִם נִזְדַּמֵּן יוֹם רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בְּשַׁבָּת,
And even if Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbos,
within the Ten Days of Teshuvah;
כִּי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא בְּחִינַת גֻּלְגַּלְתָּא,
for Rosh Hashanah is the aspect of Gulgalta, the skull,
and therefore it is called the "Head" of the year,
for it corresponds to the head
that is above the mochin within the head;
and there, there is no relevance
"If you sin, what do you do to Him?
And if your transgressions are many, what do you do to Him?"
we do not mention with the mouth
However, in the aspect of Chochmah,
although about this too it is said
"The soul You placed within me is pure,"
and no blemish can befall it
nevertheless, since the dwelling of the ruach
and there are two chambers there,
including that of "a fool's heart at his left"
which comes from the blood of the nefesh;
upon the two openings of the heart
and from this the corruption reaches
even the Chochmah in the brain,
"Above all that you guard, guard your heart,
for from it are the issues of life";
that is, from the heart flow
the issues of life to the brain.
וְעַל כֵּן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה גַּם כֵּן
included in the Ten Days of Teshuvah,
only that the teshuvah is in thought,
in the brain and heart alone,
